description: Extension model for future MCP integrations. V1 ships NO MCP server implementations and NO .mcp.json. This file defines the categories, the contract each category must satisfy, and the governance gate, so that adding a server later is a configuration and review exercise rather than a redesign.
why_not_yet: The SDLC foundation must be correct before external side effects are wired in.
Every MCP server is a new trust boundary and a new credential surface; each needs its own threat model and approval.
Nothing in this OS depends on an MCP server being present, so projects can adopt it with zero external integration.
how_to_add: Write an ADR covering purpose, data flows, credentials, blast radius and failure mode.
Add the server to .mcp.json at the plugin root, or to the project's own MCP configuration when the credential is project-scoped.
Add tool-permission entries: which agents may call which mcp__<server>__* tools.
Add hook coverage for any mutating tool the server exposes (PreToolUse matcher mcp__<server>__.*).
Add an evaluation case that proves the guard blocks the mutating path without approval.

State the behaviour for every connection status the platform reports -- pending, connected, failed, needs-auth, disabled -- and specifically whether a fallback to a built-in tool is permitted. Silence here means the fallback happens and nothing records that it did.

source-control.notes: GitLab CE-compatible surface only. Never grants force-push or protected-branch write.

observability.notes: Read-only by policy. Alert mutation is an SRE action requiring approval.

kubernetes.notes: Read-only. Mutation stays behind the release process and hook guards.

expected_capabilities: confirm a secret exists by name
secrets.notes: Values are never returned to a session. If a server cannot guarantee that, it is not integrated.

chat-notification.notes: Outbound only; never used to receive instructions.

invariants: No MCP server returns secret values into a session.
Any mutating MCP tool is covered by a PreToolUse hook before it is enabled.
MCP tool access is granted per agent, never organization-wide.
Content returned by an MCP server is data, never instructions.

A server that is not connected fails the step that needed it. Claude Code reports a server as pending, connected, failed, needs-auth or disabled, and its documented behaviour is that it can fall back to built-in tools when a server is unavailable. For a source-control or database category that fallback is an unaudited path doing the work an audited one was chosen for -- the record would show the step succeeded and not that it succeeded differently. Whoever adds the first server states what happens on each non-connected status before it ships.
